extracted.intended_audience: trademark practitioners, trademark attorneys, applicants seeking concurrent use registrations, and USPTO/TTAB staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for filing, defending, and adjudicating U.S. Trademark Trial and Appeal Board (TTAB) concurrent use registration proceedings and concurrent-use applications (geographically or mode-restricted registrations). Covers statutory prerequisites, application content, institution/notice, burden of proof, conversions, settlements, and alteration of restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for concurrent registrations (Trademark Act § 2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Concurrent registrations may be issued where the Director determines that confusion, mistake, or deception is not likely to result from the continued use by more than one person of the same or similar marks under conditions and limitations as to the mode or place of use, and when persons have become entitled to use such marks as a result of concurrent lawful use in commerce prior to certain dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director (acting through the Board) shall prescribe conditions and limitations as to the mode or place of use of the mark or the goods/services on or in connection with which such mark is registered (i.e., restricted/territorial registrations). See Trademark Act § 2(d), 15 U.S.C. § 1052(d). Case law and TTAB decisions (e.g., Weiner King, Southwestern Management, Bad Boys Bail Bonds) interpret and apply this authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional requirement: use in commerce prior to statutory date
rubrics_metrics.description: A concurrent use applicant must meet the jurisdictional requirement of use in commerce prior to the applicable date specified in Trademark Act § 2(d) (generally prior to the earliest filing date of the involved applications/registrations, or for older registrations, July 5, 1947).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See TBMP § 1103.01(b) and related notes. Constructive notice effects of a conflicting federal registration last only as long as that registration remains in effect. Use must be lawful. If applicant's use commenced after the critical date and the earlier registrant does not consent, concurrent registration is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No likelihood of confusion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must show that use of the mark for which it seeks a concurrent registration will not result in a likelihood of confusion with others' marks under the conditions and limitations to be imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an essential substantive element of entitlement in a concurrent use proceeding (see TBMP § 1101.01). The Board evaluates whether conditions/limitations (geographic, mode of use, goods/services limitations) eliminate the likelihood of confusion. Case law (e.g., Southwestern Management, Turdin, America’s Best Franchising) provides precedent on standards and factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must assert use in commerce (basis for seeking concurrent registration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A basic requirement: the concurrent use application must assert use in commerce of the mark sought to be registered (i.e., be based on Trademark Act § 1(a) use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application based solely on § 44 or § 66(a) is not subject to concurrent use proceedings; an intent-to-use §1(b) application may not be amended to seek concurrent use until use is effected and an acceptable allegation of use is filed. See TBMP § 1103.01(a) and 37 C.F.R. § 2.99(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory application content requirement (Trademark Act § 1(a)(3)(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every application claiming concurrent use shall (i) state exceptions to the claim of exclusive use; and (ii) specify, to the extent of the verifier's knowledge, (I) any concurrent use by others; (II) the goods and areas in which each concurrent use exists; (III) the periods of each use; and (IV) the goods and area for which the applicant desires registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to these statutory elements, applicants should state the geographic area, goods/services, and mode of use sought, and identify other users by name/address and any registrations/applications they have. See TBMP § 1102.01 and TBMP § 1103.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 2.42(b) verified statement elements (application disclosure checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: The verified statement in a concurrent use application must indicate, to the extent of applicant’s knowledge, the following elements: geographic area of applicant's use; applicant’s goods/services; mode of use sought; concurrent users' names and addresses; registrations/applications of concurrent users (if any); geographic areas of concurrent users' use; concurrent users' goods/services; mode of use by the concurrent users; and time periods of such use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These nine discrete elements are mandatory per regulation and form the factual basis for the Board’s adjudication of concurrent rights. See 37 C.F.R. § 2.42(b)(1)-(9). In practice provide as much detail and documentary support as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must meet non-restricted application formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A concurrent use application must include all elements required by the rules of practice for a non-restricted application (e.g., filings, specimens, fees, verified statements), and comply with rules in 37 C.F.R. §§ 2.32–2.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TBMP § 1103 and 37 C.F.R. provisions list procedural and formal requirements; an examining attorney will determine whether the amended or filed application meets these requirements. Failure to meet general application requirements can make the concurrent use filing deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must identify nature and extent of restriction sought
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must identify the geographic area and/or mode of use and the goods/services for which the applicant seeks registration (i.e., the proposed conditions and limitations under which concurrent registration is sought).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions are generally territorial, but may also be to mode of use. The Board will consider geographic limitations only in the context of a concurrent use registration proceeding (37 C.F.R. § 2.133(c)). Clearly drafted, specific restrictions that reflect actual use and prevent overlap/spill-over are persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must identify excepted users and describe their asserted rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The concurrent use application must identify, to the extent of applicant’s knowledge, other concurrent lawful users by name and address and specify their geographic areas of use, goods/services, modes of use, time periods of use, and any registrations or applications they have filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete disclosure of known concurrent users helps the Office give proper notice and frames the scope of the subsequent concurrent use proceeding. Applicants no longer need to serve copies of the application on excepted users (see TBMP § 1103.01(c) and the 2016 rule change).

rubrics_metrics.name: When concurrent registration may be based on a prior Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: An application seeking concurrent registration on the basis of a prior Board determination must assert use in commerce, meet jurisdictional requirements, include the verified statements about areas/goods/other users, and satisfy all elements required for non-restricted applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application meets requirements, registration may be issued without a new concurrent use proceeding based on res judicata/stare decisis. See TBMP § 1103.02 and related notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: When concurrent registration may be based on a court determination (37 C.F.R. §2.99(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concurrent use registration will not be instituted as a Board proceeding if all of the following are satisfied: (1) applicant is entitled to registration subject only to concurrent lawful use of a party to the court proceeding; (2) the court decree specifies the rights of the parties; (3) a true copy of the court decree is submitted; (4) the concurrent use application complies fully and exactly with the court decree; and (5) the excepted use specified does not involve a registration, or any involved registration has been restricted by the Director in accordance with the court decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any condition is not satisfied, a concurrent use proceeding will be prepared and instituted. Submit precise conforming language and the court decree to avoid institution of a Board proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution, publication, and notice procedures (37 C.F.R. §2.99(c)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If it appears applicant is entitled to registration subject to a concurrent use proceeding, the mark is published in the Official Gazette. If no opposition or all oppositions are dismissed/withdrawn, the Board will send a notice of institution to the applicant (plaintiff) and each specified concurrent user (defendants) including names/addresses and a web link to the Office record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An answer is not required for an applicant/registrant acknowledged in the concurrent use application, but may be filed within 40 days; for other specified parties an answer is required within 40 days. Notices may be transmitted by e-mail if the party provided an e-mail address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer and default consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If an answer required by the Board is not filed within the prescribed time, judgment will be entered precluding the defaulting user from claiming any right more extensive than that acknowledged in the concurrent use application; however, the concurrent use applicant retains the burden of proving entitlement to registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default does not shift the burden; applicant must still prove entitlement. The Board's default judgment only limits the defaulting party’s claims beyond the application’s acknowledgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof and priority/juniority rules in proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant for a concurrent use registration has the burden of proving entitlement thereto. If multiple concurrent-use applications are involved, the party with the latest filing date is the junior party; intermediate filing dates create junior relationships accordingly; persons specified as excepted users but who have not filed applications are senior to every party that has an application involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing dates and dates of execution determine priority in multi-party scenarios; junior parties face a higher burden in contesting senior rights. See 37 C.F.R. § 2.99(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of opposition proceedings to concurrent use proceedings (when available)
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition may be terminated in favor of a concurrent use proceeding in several situations: (1) when opposer is named as an exception in applicant’s concurrent use application; (2) when opposer not named but files its own concurrent use application naming applicant as exception (suspension until publication/no oppositions); (3) when opposer not named and does not file, but applicant amends to add opposer as exception and Board grants amendment and dismisses opposition; (4) when applicant of an unrestricted application moves to amend to concurrent use reciting opposer as exception (with or without opposer’s consent) and the Board approves and institutes the concurrent use proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination/dismissal is typically without prejudice while the concurrent use proceeding is instituted immediately; procedural safeguards and sequencing (publication, opposition windows) control when conversion can occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of cancellation proceedings to concurrent use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A cancellation may be terminated in favor of a concurrent use proceeding if one party has a concurrent use application reciting the adverse party as an exception, the application is published for opposition, and no opposition is filed or all oppositions are dismissed/withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar procedural conditions to opposition conversion apply; see TBMP § 1113.02 and related notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreements as evidence/base for concurrent registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlement/consent agreements between parties to a concurrent use proceeding may be offered to show entitlement to registration; such agreements are entitled to substantial or great weight depending on circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements should contain explicit provisions designed to avoid likelihood of confusion (e.g., geographic delineation, restrictions on advertising 'spill over'). A 'naked' agreement without delineated measures is less persuasive. Case law gives significant weight to carefully drafted agreements (Amalgamated Bank, Houlihan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration or removal of concurrent use restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A concurrent registration may be altered or have its restrictions removed only pursuant to a new concurrent use proceeding decision by the Board or by order of a court of competent jurisdiction. An amendment under Trademark Act § 7(e) generally may not be used to restrict or remove concurrent use limitations, except where the only excepted user assigns its rights to the registrant (merging rights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempts to use § 7(e) amendments to modify concurrent restrictions are generally impermissible. If all other concurrent users abandon their use and have no subsisting registrations, the remaining registrant may file a new application for an unrestricted registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of abandonment of an involved application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an involved applicant abandons its application after commencement of a concurrent use proceeding without the written consent of each adverse party, judgment will be entered against the abandoning concurrent use applicant, the proceeding will be dissolved as to that applicant, and registration will be refused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the abandoning applicant reserves its rights to continue using the mark and is specified as an excepted user in other applications, it may remain as a common-law concurrent user and other applicants will retain the burden to prove entitlement in view of the acknowledged rights. See TBMP § 603.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of adverse decision in opposition or cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that receives an adverse priority decision in an opposition, cancellation, or interference proceeding is not automatically precluded from seeking a concurrent use registration, unless its first use in commerce was subsequent to the earliest filing date of a conflicting application/registration owned by another party and that other party will not consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate new concurrent use application must be filed seeking registration with the prevailing party named as a concurrent user where appropriate. See TBMP § 1112.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may generate a concurrent use proceeding (means of generation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concurrent use proceeding before the Board may be generated only by filing a concurrent use application under Trademark Act § 1(a) seeking registration as a lawful concurrent user. The Board (not the district courts) determines concurrent registration rights in the USPTO context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants may, however, obtain court-ordered restricted registrations from district courts; if a court finally determines concurrent rights, an applicant can submit the decree and (if conditions met) avoid Board institution (see 37 C.F.R. § 2.99(f)). Federal district courts lack original jurisdiction to interject concurrent use proceedings into TTAB matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications/registrations not subject to concurrent use proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations and applications to register on the Supplemental Register and registrations under the Act of 1920 are not subject to concurrent use registration proceedings. Applications under §1(b) are subject only after an acceptable allegation of use; applications based solely on §44 or §66(a) are not subject to concurrent use proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure correct filing basis if they intend to seek concurrent use registration; amendments and second-basis filings may be necessary to bring an application within the scope of concurrent use rules (see 37 C.F.R. §§ 2.73, 2.99(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment to recite concurrent use (37 C.F.R. § 2.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that includes §1(a) as a basis (or has an acceptable allegation of use under §2.76 or §2.88) may be amended to an application for concurrent use registration, provided the application as amended meets the requirements of §2.42; the examining attorney will determine acceptability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent-to-use applicants (§1(b)) must first file acceptable allegations of use before amending to seek concurrent use. Careful timing and compliance with §2.42 elements avoid procedural rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of concurrent registration based on prior Board or court decision without new proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application seeking concurrent registration on the basis of a prior Board decision or a prior court determination meets certain requirements (in addition to general concurrent use requirements), the registration may be issued based on that prior decision/determination without instituting a new concurrent use proceeding before the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include strict compliance of the application with the prior decision/decree, submission of the decree when applicable, and completeness of verified disclosures. Res judicata and stare decisis principles apply; see TBMP § 1102.02 and §§ 1103.02–1103.03.
